blocks.text: B1-02 · The verbal forms I/X
Lesson overview

In A2 you have combined the forms II and III well (A2-17) and you have learned to recognize the forms IV"X (A2-18). In this unity, you move from recognition to use: you combine all forms, from I to X, in all people and in all ways (perfect, imperfect, conjunctive, juxt, imperative); it forms participles; and maṣdar; learn to predict the meaning of a derivative form from the root. We only work with healthy roots: weak verbs in derived forms are the subject of B1-06. Three weeks.

rows: 15–17 hours · three weeks (weeks 97–99), plus the EGY track in separate blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, dictionary by root, Grammar G42, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. form perfect, imperfect, imperative, participles and maṣdar the forms of a healthy root;
2. to combine any derived form in all persons, the conjunctive and the juxive;
3. properly vocalize a derived verb written without voice;
4. distinguish union hamza (forms VII, VIII, IX, X) and cutting hamza (form IV);
5. predict the probable meaning of a derived form and verify it in the dictionary;
6. use in context the most frequent derived verbs of the newspaper language.
Three-week plan.

9. Pronunciation

The doubles of forms II and V. ⁧دَرَّسَ⁩ , ⁧تَعَلَّمَ⁩ , ⁧تَحَدَّثَ⁩ : the second double radical must be held, otherwise feel another form ( ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ ). Exercise in pairs: darasa / darrasa, ʿalima / ʿallama. The ā Forms III and VI. ⁧سَاعَدَ⁩ , ⁧تَعَاوَنَ⁩ , ⁧تَفَاوَضَ⁩ : The long vowel after the first radical is the sign of form. Elongate it decisively. The t of form VIII. iǧtamaʿa, iqtaraḥa, intaḫaba: the t comes after the first radical. Don't move it: iǧtamaʿa, not *itǧamaʿa.
